text:
Rita: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — I sketched an alternative to the soft-lease model: an adaptive epoch-credit ledger + cheap probe tokens. Goal: fast edge admission, central eventual fairness, and easier abuse throttling. Thoughts?

Sam: Curious — how do credits get reconciled? is this purely central authoritative or do edges keep a transient view?

Rita: Edges keep a transient view (local credits) for O(10ms) fast-path admission. Central ledger reconciles every epoch (10s) and issues corrective adjustments. Local credits are conservative to avoid overspend.

Jess: Nice. That matches our perf needs. Two followups: 1) how do we prevent clients from replaying/parallelizing to drain multiple edges? 2) what’s the penalty shape for repeated bursts?

Kai: For (1) add client-scoped probe tokens + origin fuzzing (randomized epoch boundaries per-client-subnet). For (2) use a polynomial decay penalty on burst score (e.g., penalty ~ (burst_factor^1.5)) so the first burst is cheap but sustained bursts escalate nonlinearly.

Rita: Agreed. Proposal details: epoch = 10s (configurable), base replenishment = quota_rate * epoch, burst_bucket = min(base * 3, absolute_hard_cap), probe_rate = 0.5% of requests (can be adaptive). Probes carry a signed short-lived nonce so central can attribute cost later. If a probe fails attribution we mark it suspicious and decrement reputation.

Sam: Can you paste the rough config/pseudocode for the admission decision?

Rita: Sure — config sketch: 

```json
{
  "epoch_secs": 10,
  "base_multiplier": 1.0,
  "burst_multiplier": 3.0,
  "probe_pct": 0.005,
  "penalty_exponent": 1.5,
  "fallback_model": "small-v1",
  "unknown_client_policy": "soft-queue-low-cpu"
}
```

And admission pseudo: 
1) if local_credit >= cost_estimate: allow
2) else if is_probe and probe_quota > 0: allow + tag
3) else if central_recent_balance_estimate >= cost_estimate: allow, decrement local soft-credit
4) else route to fallback_model or queue with tokenized backoff

Jess: We need telemetry hooks: cost_estimate should incorporate model, tokens, and early-stop heuristics. Add a histogram for estimated_cost vs actual_tokens_consumed to tune the estimator.

Kai: Also add a safety: if client reputation falls below threshold, drop probes and switch to strict per-request admission (no bursts) and emit incident for review.

ops-bot: Deployment queued: canary=5% -> target groups: edge-us-east-1, edge-eu-west-1. CI: green ✅

Sam: :thumbsup:

Jess: I'll own a synthetic test plan: will create a mixed workload (100k requests over 10min) with 6 attack shapes (parallel replay, short-burst, long-burst, big-payload, probe-evasion, model-switch). Will measure fairness index, false-positive rate, and 95th p99 tail latency.

Rita: TL;DR for rollout: start canary 5% (2 regions) -> monitor fairness index & suspicious rate -> increase to 25% with stricter penalty exponent if suspicious rate < 0.1% -> full rollout. Need signoffs: Sam (perf), Jess (telemetry/tests), Kai (security).

Kai: I can sign off if we add the origin fuzzing and the reputation circuit breaker. One comment: make penalty_exponent tunable via remote config.

Jess: Agree, will add dashboards and a synthetic baseline job. Taking ownership of rollout PR.

Rita: Thanks — I'll update the RFC with these details and attach the config sketch. If anyone has objections to the conservative default numbers above speak up now, otherwise I'll open the canary PR after test infra is ready. :rocket:
